main.description: A tag applied to some other record, in ANY lexicon -- Jason's explicit requirement (2026-09-22): tags must cross lexicons, not be a per-record-type feature reimplemented for messages, documents, profiles, and anything else separately. One Tag type does this because 'subject' names a record by author + collection + rkey together (not just author + rkey the way network.essmesh.governance.signal's subject or network.essmesh.chat.message's replyTo do -- those only ever point within their own collection, so they don't need to say which collection; a cross-lexicon tag does). Append-only, same shape as network.essmesh.chat.message: every tag mints its own key, so any writer can tag any record without coordinating with anyone else or needing write access to the tagged record itself -- tagging something never mutates it.

subject.description: '{authorHex}/{collection}/{rkey}' naming the tagged record -- see records::record_ref in the core crate. Not a strongRef/CID reference (no content-addressing here, unlike signal.subject) -- a tag names a specific record slot, not a specific version of it.
